units.zh: 克讓，武皇之仲弟也。
units.en: Ke Rang was Li Keyong's second younger brother.
units.literal: Ke Rang was the Martial Emperor's second younger brother.

units.zh: 少善騎射，以勇悍聞。
units.en: From youth he was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and his reputation rested on bold, ferocious fighting.
units.literal: In youth he excelled at mounted archery and was known for fierce courage.

units.zh: 咸通中，從討龐勳，以功為振武都校。
units.en: In the Xiantong era he took part in the suppression of Pang Xun and, for his service, was appointed metropolitan commandant of Zhenwu.
units.literal: During the Xiantong period he followed the campaign against Pang Xun and, for merit, was made metropolitan commandant of Zhenwu.

units.zh: 乾符中，王仙芝陷荊、襄，朝廷征兵，克讓率師奉詔，賊平，以功授金吾將軍，留宿衛。
units.en: In the Qianfu era, after Wang Xianzhi overran Jing and Xiang, the court mobilized troops. Ke Rang led his forces as ordered, and when the rebels were crushed he was made general of the Golden Guard and kept on palace guard duty.
units.literal: During Qianfu, Wang Xianzhi seized Jing and Xiang. The court raised troops; Ke Rang led his army in obedience to the edict. When the bandits were pacified, he was appointed general of the Golden Guard and remained on palace night duty.

units.zh: 初，懿祖歸朝，憲宗賜宅於親仁坊，自長慶以來，相次一人典衛兵。
units.en: When the Virtuous Ancestor (Yizu) first submitted to the Tang court, Emperor Xianzong granted the family a residence in Qinren Ward. From the Changqing reign onward, a member of the clan in each generation held command of the palace guard.
units.literal: Earlier, when the Founding Ancestor returned to court allegiance, Emperor Xianzong granted a residence in Qinren Ward. From the Changqing era onward, one after another held command of the guard troops.

units.zh: 武皇之起雲中，殺段文楚，朝議罪之，命加兵於我，懼，將逃歸，天子詔巡使王處存夜圍親仁坊捕克讓。
units.en: When Li Keyong rose in Yunzhong and killed Duan Wenchu, the court condemned him and ordered troops sent against the clan. Fearing arrest, he prepared to flee north, and the emperor ordered the commissioner Wang Chucun to surround Qinren Ward by night and capture Ke Rang.
units.literal: When the Martial Emperor rose in Yunzhong and killed Duan Wenchu, court opinion condemned him and ordered additional troops against us. In fear, about to flee home, the Son of Heaven ordered the circuit commissioner Wang Chucun to surround Qinren Ward by night and seize Ke Rang.

units.zh: 詰旦兵合，克讓與紀綱何相溫、安文寬、石的曆十餘騎彎弧躍馬，突圍而出。
units.en: At daybreak the encircling force closed in. Ke Rang, with his officers He Xiangwen, An Wenkuan, Shi Deli, and a dozen horsemen, strung their bows, spurred their mounts, and charged out of the trap.
units.literal: At dawn the troops closed in. Ke Rang, with his commanders He Xiangwen, An Wenkuan, Shi Deli, and more than ten riders, bent their bows, spurred their horses, and broke through the encirclement.

units.zh: 官軍數千人追之，比至渭橋，死者數百。
units.en: Several thousand government troops gave chase, and by the time the pursuit reached Wei Bridge, several hundred men lay dead.
units.literal: Several thousand government troops pursued them; by the time they reached Wei Bridge, several hundred had been killed.

units.zh: 克讓自夏陽掠船而濟，歸於雁門。
units.en: Ke Rang commandeered boats at Xiayang, crossed the river, and made his way back to Yanmen.
units.literal: Ke Rang seized boats at Xiayang and crossed the river, returning to Yanmen.

units.zh: 明年，武皇昭雪，克讓復入宿衛。
units.en: The following year, after Li Keyong was cleared of the charges against him, Ke Rang returned to palace guard service.
units.literal: The next year, after the Martial Emperor was cleared of blame, Ke Rang again entered palace night duty.

units.zh: 黃巢犯闕，僖宗幸蜀，克讓時守潼關，為賊所敗，以部下六七騎伏於南山佛寺，夜為山僧所害。
units.en: When Huang Chao stormed the capital and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Ke Rang was holding Tong Pass. Routed by the rebels, he took refuge with only six or seven riders in a temple on South Mountain, where mountain monks killed him that night.
units.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital and Emperor Xizong fled to Shu, Ke Rang was then defending Tong Pass. Defeated by the rebels, he hid with six or seven horsemen of his command in a Buddhist temple on South Mountain, and that night was killed by mountain monks.

units.zh: 克讓既死，紀綱渾進通冒刃獲免，歸於黃巢。
units.en: After Ke Rang's death, his officer Hun Jintong fought through the blades and survived, then went over to Huang Chao's side.
units.literal: After Ke Rang died, his commander Hun Jintong braved the blades and escaped, going over to Huang Chao.

units.zh: 中和二年冬，武皇入關討賊，屯沙苑。
units.en: In the winter of Zhonghe 2, Li Keyong marched through the passes against the rebels and encamped at Shayuan.
units.literal: In the winter of the second year of Zhonghe, the Martial Emperor entered the passes to attack the rebels and encamped at Shayuan.

units.zh: 黃巢遣使米重威齎賂修好，因送渾進通至，兼擒送害克讓僧十人。
units.en: Huang Chao sent Mi Chongwei with gifts to sue for peace, returned Hun Jintong with the embassy, and also delivered up the ten monks who had murdered Ke Rang.
units.literal: Huang Chao sent the envoy Mi Chongwei bearing gifts to seek peace, and with him sent Hun Jintong back, together with the ten monks who had killed Ke Rang, seized and delivered up.

units.zh: 武皇燔偽詔，還其使，盡誅諸僧，為克讓發哀行服，悲慟久之。
units.en: Li Keyong burned Huang Chao's forged edict, sent the envoy away, had all the monks executed, and for Ke Rang observed mourning and wore funeral dress, grieving for a long while.
units.literal: The Martial Emperor burned the false edict, sent the envoy back, executed all the monks, and for Ke Rang held mourning and wore mourning garments, grieving deeply for a long time.

units.zh: 克修，字崇遠，武皇從父弟也。
units.en: Ke Xiu, styled Chongyuan, was Li Keyong's younger cousin.
units.literal: Ke Xiu, styled Chongyuan, was the Martial Emperor's younger cousin.

units.zh: 父德成，初為天寧軍使，從獻祖討龐勳，以功授朔州刺史。
units.en: His father Decheng had first served as military commissioner of Tianning. He followed the Offering Ancestor against Pang Xun and, for his service, was made prefect of Shuozhou.
units.literal: His father Decheng was first military commissioner of Tianning. He followed the Offering Ancestor in the campaign against Pang Xun and, for merit, was appointed prefect of Shuozhou.

units.zh: 克修少便弓馬，從父征討，所至立功，武皇節制雁門，以克修為奉誠軍使，從入關為前鋒，破黃揆於華陰，敗尚讓於梁田坡，蹙黃巢於光順門，每戰皆捷，勇懾諸軍。
units.en: Ke Xiu was skilled with bow and horse from youth. On his father's campaigns he distinguished himself wherever he fought. When Li Keyong took command of Yanmen, he appointed Ke Xiu commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. Marching into the passes as vanguard, Ke Xiu defeated Huang Kui at Huayin, routed Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope, and drove Huang Chao back at Guangshun Gate. He won every engagement, and his boldness overawed the other armies.
units.literal: Ke Xiu from youth was adept with bow and horse. Following his father on campaigns, wherever he went he achieved merit. When the Martial Emperor held military authority over Yanmen, he made Ke Xiu commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. Following him into the passes as vanguard, he defeated Huang Kui at Huayin, routed Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope, and pressed Huang Chao at Guangshun Gate. In every battle he was victorious, and his courage awed all the armies.

units.zh: 賊平，以功檢校刑部尚書，為左營軍使。
units.en: After the rebels were crushed, he was made acting minister of justice and commander of the Left Camp Army for his achievements.
units.literal: When the rebels were pacified, for merit he was made acting minister of justice and commander of the Left Camp Army.

units.zh: 其年十月，潞州牙將安居受來乞師，請復昭義軍，武皇遣大將賀公雅、李筠、安金俊等以兵從。
units.en: In the tenth month of that year, the Lu garrison officer An Jushou came to request aid in restoring the Zhaoyi command. Li Keyong sent the senior generals He Gongya, Li Jun, An Jinjun, and others with an army in support.
units.literal: That year in the tenth month, the Lu prefecture garrison officer An Jushou came to request troops, asking to restore the Zhaoyi army. The Martial Emperor sent the great generals He Gongya, Li Jun, An Jinjun, and others with troops to follow.

units.zh: 與孟方立戰於銅鞮，不利，武皇乃令克修將兵繼進。
units.en: The allied force fought Meng Fangli at Tongdi without success, so Li Keyong ordered Ke Xiu to advance with reinforcements.
units.literal: They fought Meng Fangli at Tongdi with an unfavorable outcome, and the Martial Emperor then ordered Ke Xiu to lead troops forward in succession.

units.zh: 是月，平潞州，斬其刺史李殷銳，乃表克修為昭義節度使。
units.en: That month Luzhou was taken, its prefect Li Yinrui was executed, and Ke Xiu was recommended for appointment as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: That month they pacified Luzhou, beheaded its prefect Li Yinrui, and then memorialized to appoint Ke Xiu military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 光啟二年九月，克修出師山東，收復邢、洺。
units.en: In the ninth month of Guangqi 2, Ke Xiu took the field east of the Taihang range and recovered Xing and Ming.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Guangqi, Ke Xiu marched east of the mountains and recovered Xing and Ming.

units.zh: 十一月，拔故鎮。
units.en: In the eleventh month he took Guzhen.
units.literal: In the eleventh month he captured Guzhen.

units.zh: 孟方立遣將呂臻來援，戰於焦崗，大敗之，擒呂臻，俘斬萬計，進拔武安、臨洺諸屬縣，乘勝進圍邢州。
units.en: Meng Fangli sent Lü Zhen to the rescue. Ke Xiu met him at Jiaogang and won a crushing victory, capturing Lü Zhen and killing or taking prisoner tens of thousands. He then seized Wu'an, Linming, and the other subordinate counties and, riding the momentum, laid siege to Xingzhou.
units.literal: Meng Fangli sent the general Lü Zhen to relieve him. They fought at Jiaogang and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Lü Zhen. Captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands. Advancing, they took Wu'an, Linming, and other subordinate counties, and pressing the victory moved to besiege Xingzhou.

units.zh: 方立求援於鎮州，王鎔出師三萬援之，克修軍退。
units.en: Fangli appealed to Zhenzhou for help. Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army fell back.
units.literal: Fangli sought aid from Zhenzhou; Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army withdrew.

units.zh: 及李罕之來歸，武皇授以澤州刺史，與克修合勢進攻河陽，連歲出師，以苦懷、孟。
units.en: When Li Hanzhi defected to Li Keyong, he was made prefect of Zezhou and joined Ke Xiu in a combined offensive against Heyang. Campaigning year after year, they wore down the Huai and Meng factions.
units.literal: When Li Hanzhi came over to our side, the Martial Emperor appointed him prefect of Zezhou. Together with Ke Xiu he combined forces to attack Heyang, campaigning year after year to wear down Huai and Meng.

units.zh: 文德元年十月，孟方立遣將奚忠信將兵三萬襲我遼州，克修設伏於遼之東山，大敗賊軍，擒忠信以獻。
units.en: In the tenth month of Wende 1, Meng Fangli sent Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men to raid Liaozhou. Ke Xiu laid an ambush on East Mountain and routed the enemy, capturing Zhongxin and sending him to headquarters.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Wende, Meng Fangli sent the general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to raid our Liaozhou. Ke Xiu set an ambush on East Mountain of Liao and inflicted a great defeat on the rebel army, capturing Zhongxin and presenting him.

units.zh: 龍紀元年，武皇大舉以伐邢、洺，及班師，因撫封於上黨。
units.en: In Longji 1, Li Keyong mounted a major campaign against Xing and Ming. When the army returned, he rewarded and enfeoffed his followers at Shangdang.
units.literal: In the first year of Longji, the Martial Emperor launched a major campaign against Xing and Ming. When the army returned, he therefore bestowed rewards and enfeoffments at Shangdang.

units.zh: 克修性儉嗇，不事華靡，供帳饔膳，品數簡陋。
units.en: Ke Xiu was frugal by nature and shunned display. His quarters and table were spare and plain.
units.literal: Ke Xiu by nature was frugal and sparing, not given to luxury. His furnishings and meals were few and plain in kind and number.

units.zh: 武皇怒其菲薄，笞而詬之，克修慚憤發疾；
units.en: Li Keyong, angry at his austerity, had him flogged and berated him. Ke Xiu, mortified and embittered, fell ill;
units.literal: The Martial Emperor, angered at his meagerness, flogged and reviled him. Ke Xiu, ashamed and resentful, fell ill;

units.zh: 明年三月，卒於潞之府第，時年三十一。
units.en: and in the third month of the following year he died at the Lu prefectural residence, aged thirty-one.
units.literal: in the third month of the following year he died in the prefectural residence at Lu, aged thirty-one.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，追贈太師。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong came to the throne, Ke Xiu was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 克修子二人，長曰嗣弼，次曰嗣肱。
units.en: Ke Xiu had two sons: the elder, Sibi, and the younger, Sigu.
units.literal: Ke Xiu had two sons: the elder was Sibi, the younger Sigu.

units.zh: 嗣弼初授澤州刺史，曆昭義、橫海節度副使，改海州刺史。
units.en: Sibi was first made prefect of Zezhou, then served as deputy commissioner of Zhaoyi and Henghai in turn, and was later transferred to prefect of Haizhou.
units.literal: Sibi was first appointed prefect of Zezhou, then served successively as deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi and Henghai, and was later transferred to prefect of Haizhou.

units.zh: 天祐十九年，契丹犯燕、趙，陷涿郡，
units.en: In Tianyou 19 the Khitan invaded Yan and Zhao and took Zhuo commandery,
units.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tianyou, the Khitan invaded Yan and Zhao and seized Zhuo commandery,

units.zh: 〈（《遼史·太祖紀》：十二月癸亥，圍涿州，有白兔緣壘而上，是日破其郛。）〉
units.en: (From the 《History of Liao·Basic Annals of Taizu》: On the guihai day of the twelfth month they besieged Zhuozhou. A white hare climbed the ramparts, and that same day they breached the outer wall.)〉
units.literal: (From the 《History of Liao·Basic Annals of Taizu》: On the guihai day of the twelfth month they besieged Zhuozhou. A white hare climbed the ramparts, and that day they breached the outer wall.)〉

units.zh: 嗣弼舉家被俘，遷於幕庭。
units.en: Sibi and his whole household were taken captive and removed to the Khitan court.
units.literal: Sibi's entire household was captured and removed to the Khitan court.

units.zh: 嗣肱，少有膽略，屢立戰功，夾城之役，從周德威為前鋒。
units.en: Sigu showed daring and strategic sense from youth and won repeated distinction in battle. In the Jiacheng campaign he served under Zhou Dewei as vanguard.
units.literal: Sigu from youth had daring and resourcefulness and repeatedly achieved military merit. In the Jiacheng campaign he followed Zhou Dewei as vanguard.

units.zh: 時兄嗣弼為昭義副使，與嗣昭守城，兄弟內外奮戰，忠力威壯，感動三軍。
units.en: His elder brother Sibi was then deputy commissioner of Zhaoyi and, with Sizhao, held the city. The brothers fought fiercely inside and out, their loyalty and prowess so imposing that they stirred the whole army.
units.literal: At the time his elder brother Sibi was deputy commissioner of Zhaoyi; with Sizhao he defended the city. The brothers fought fiercely within and without, their loyalty and strength majestic and inspiring, moving all three armies.

units.zh: 潞圍既解，以功授檢校左僕射，入為三城巡檢，知衙內事。
units.en: After the siege of Lu was raised, he was made acting left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat for his service. He entered the capital as inspector of the Three Cities and took charge of inner yamen affairs.
units.literal: When the siege of Lu was lifted, for merit he was appointed acting left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat. He entered the capital as inspector of the Three Cities and managed affairs within the yamen.

units.zh: 天祐七年，周德威援靈、夏，党項阻道，音驛不通。
units.en: In Tianyou 7, Zhou Dewei marched to relieve Ling and Xia. The Tangut blocked the route, and no word came through the courier network.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei went to relieve Ling and Xia. The Tangut blocked the road, and courier communications ceased.

units.zh: 嗣肱奉命自麟州渡河，應接德威，與党項轉戰數十里，合德威軍。
units.en: Sigu was ordered to cross from Linzhou and link up with Dewei. After fighting the Tangut over several tens of li, he joined Dewei's force.
units.literal: Sigu received orders to cross the river from Linzhou and link up with Dewei. Fighting the Tangut over several tens of li, he joined Dewei's army.

units.zh: 柏鄉之戰，嗣肱為馬步都虞候。
units.en: At Baixiang, Sigu served as chief controller of horse and foot.
units.literal: In the battle of Baixiang, Sigu served as chief controller of horse and foot.

units.zh: 明年，從莊宗會朱友謙於猗氏，改教練使，與存審援河中，敗汴軍於胡壁堡，獲將龐讓。
units.en: The following year he accompanied Emperor Zhuangzong to meet Zhu Youqian at Yishi and was made training commissioner. With Cunshen he marched to relieve Hezhong, defeated the Liang army at Hubi Fort, and captured the general Pang Rang.
units.literal: The next year he followed Emperor Zhuangzong to meet Zhu Youqian at Yishi, was transferred to training commissioner, and with Cunshen went to relieve Hezhong, defeating the Bian army at Hubi Fort and capturing the general Pang Rang.

units.zh: 十年，與存審屯趙州，擊汴人於觀津。
units.en: In the tenth year he encamped at Zhaozhou with Cunshen and attacked the Liang forces at Guanjin.
units.literal: In the tenth year he encamped at Zhaozhou with Cunshen and struck the Bian troops at Guanjin.

units.zh: 時梁祖新屠棗強，其將賀德倫急攻蓚縣，率師五萬合勢營於蓚之西。
units.en: The Liang founder had just slaughtered the population of Zaoqiang. His general He Delun was pressing the attack on Suo county and had brought fifty thousand men to encamp west of the city in a combined force.
units.literal: At the time the Liang founder had newly massacred Zaoqiang. His general He Delun pressed the attack on Suo county and led fifty thousand men in combined strength to encamp west of Suo.

units.zh: 嗣肱自下博率騎三百，薄晚與梁之樵芻者相雜，日既晡，入梁軍營門，諸騎相合，大噪，弧矢星發，虓闞馳突。
units.en: Sigu led three hundred horsemen from Xiabo. Near dusk he mixed in with Liang men out gathering firewood and fodder. In the late afternoon he rode through the Liang camp gate. His horsemen closed up, raised a deafening uproar, loosed arrows in a storm, and charged roaring through the encampment.
units.literal: Sigu led three hundred horsemen from Xiabo. Toward evening he mingled with the Liang foragers gathering firewood and fodder. After the sun had passed mid-afternoon he entered the Liang army's camp gate. The horsemen converged, raised a great clamor, arrows flew like stars, and with fierce shouts they charged and broke through.

units.zh: 汴人不知所為，營中擾，既暝，斂騎而退。
units.en: The Liang troops did not know what had hit them, and the camp fell into chaos. After dark he gathered his riders and withdrew.
units.literal: The Bian men did not know what to do; the camp was thrown into disorder. When night fell, he gathered his riders and withdrew.

units.zh: 是夜，梁祖燒營而遁，解蓚縣之圍。
units.en: That night the Liang founder burned his camp and fled, lifting the siege of Suo.
units.literal: That night the Liang founder burned his camp and fled, lifting the siege of Suo county.

units.zh: 以功特授蔚州刺史、雁門以北都知兵馬使。
units.en: For this exploit he was specially appointed prefect of Weizhou and commander of all forces north of Yanmen.
units.literal: For merit he was specially appointed prefect of Weizhou and commander of all military forces north of Yanmen.

units.zh: 從平劉守光。
units.en: He took part in the campaign that brought down Liu Shouguang.
units.literal: He followed in the pacification of Liu Shouguang.

units.zh: 十二年，改應州刺史，累遷澤、代二州刺史、石嶺以北都知兵馬使。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was made prefect of Yingzhou and was later promoted in turn to prefect of Ze and Dai and commander of all forces north of Shiling Pass.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou, and was promoted in succession to prefect of Ze and Dai and commander of all military forces north of Shiling.

units.zh: 十九年，新州刺史王鬱叛入契丹。
units.en: In the nineteenth year Wang Yu, prefect of Xinzhou, rebelled and defected to the Khitan.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year, Wang Yu, prefect of Xinzhou, rebelled and went over to the Khitan.

units.zh: 嗣肱進兵定媯、儒、武等三州，授山北都團練使。
units.en: Sigu advanced and pacified Gui, Ru, and Wu, and was appointed regimental commissioner of the Northern Mountains.
units.literal: Sigu advanced his troops and pacified the three prefectures of Gui, Ru, and Wu, and was appointed regimental commissioner of the Northern Mountains.

units.zh: 二十年春，卒於新州，時年四十五。
units.en: In the spring of the twentieth year he died at Xinzhou, aged forty-five.
units.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he died at Xinzhou, aged forty-five.

units.zh: 克恭，武皇之諸弟也。
units.en: Ke Gong was one of Li Keyong's younger brothers.
units.literal: Ke Gong was one of the Martial Emperor's younger brothers.

units.zh: 龍紀中，為決勝軍使。
units.en: During the Longji era he served as commissioner of the Decisive Victory Army.
units.literal: During Longji he was commissioner of the Decisive Victory Army.

units.zh: 大順初，潞帥李克修卒，克恭代為昭義節度使。
units.en: Early in the Dashun era, after the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, Ke Gong succeeded him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: At the beginning of Dazhun, the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, and Ke Gong replaced him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 性驕橫不法，未閑軍政。
units.en: He was arrogant, lawless, and wholly unversed in military administration.
units.literal: By nature he was arrogant, overbearing, and lawless, and unversed in military administration.

units.zh: 潞人素便克修之簡正，惡克恭之恣縱，又以克修非罪暴卒，人士離心。
units.en: The people of Lu had long valued Ke Xiu's plain, upright rule and resented Ke Gong's excesses. Ke Xiu's sudden death, though he was innocent of wrongdoing, also alienated the gentry and commoners.
units.literal: The people of Lu had long been accustomed to Ke Xiu's simplicity and rectitude and hated Ke Gong's wanton indulgence. Moreover, because Ke Xiu had died violently though guiltless, officials and commoners lost heart.

units.zh: 時武皇初定邢、洺三州，將有事於河朔，大搜軍實。
units.en: Li Keyong had just secured Xing, Ming, and the third prefecture and was preparing for operations in Hebei, so he made a sweeping levy of military supplies.
units.literal: At the time the Martial Emperor had newly pacified the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and another, was about to undertake operations in Hebei, and made a great levy of military stores.

units.zh: 潞州有後院軍，兵之雄勁者，克恭選其五百人獻於武皇，軍使安居受惜其兵。
units.en: Lu maintained a Rear Court Army of its toughest troops. Ke Gong selected five hundred of them and sent them to Li Keyong. The army commissioner An Jushou resented losing his best men.
units.literal: Lu had a Rear Court Army of the strongest troops. Ke Gong selected five hundred of them and presented them to the Martial Emperor. The army commissioner An Jushou regretted the loss of his troops.

units.zh: 不悅。
units.en: He was deeply displeased.
units.literal: He was displeased.

units.zh: 克恭令裨校李元審、安建、紀綱、馮霸部送太原，行次銅鞮縣，馮霸劫眾謀叛，殺都將劉杲、縣令戴勞謙，循山而南，比及沁水，有眾三千。
units.en: Ke Gong ordered the subordinate officers Li Yuanshen, An Jian, the escort officers, and Feng Ba to march the detachment to Taiyuan. At Tongdi county Feng Ba incited a mutiny, killed the commander Liu Gao and the magistrate Dai Laoqian, and led his men south along the mountains until, by the time they reached Qinshui, he had three thousand followers.
units.literal: Ke Gong ordered the subordinate officers Li Yuanshen, An Jian, the commanders, and Feng Ba to escort them to Taiyuan. When they reached Tongdi county, Feng Ba incited the troops to rebel, killed the commander Liu Gao and the magistrate Dai Laoqian, followed the mountains southward, and by the time they reached Qinshui had three thousand followers.

units.zh: 武皇令李元審將兵擊之，與霸戰於沁水，不利，元審戰傷，收軍於潞。
units.en: Li Keyong ordered Li Yuanshen to attack them. Yuanshen fought Feng Ba at Qinshui without success, was wounded, and withdrew to Lu.
units.literal: The Martial Emperor ordered Li Yuanshen to lead troops against him. He fought Feng Ba at Qinshui with an unfavorable outcome; Yuanshen was wounded in battle and withdrew the army to Lu.

units.zh: 五月十五日，克恭視元審於孔目吏劉崇之第。
units.en: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month Ke Gong went to visit the wounded Yuanshen at the home of the clerical officer Liu Chong.
units.literal: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month, Ke Gong visited Yuanshen at the residence of the clerical officer Liu Chong.

units.zh: 是日，州將安居受引兵仗攻克恭，因風縱火，克恭、元審並遇害，州民推居受為留後。
units.en: That same day the prefectural officer An Jushou led armed men against Ke Gong, set fires with the wind at his back, and killed both Ke Gong and Yuanshen. The people of the prefecture made Jushou acting commissioner.
units.literal: That day the prefectural officer An Jushou led armed troops to attack and overcome Ke Gong. Taking advantage of the wind he set fires. Ke Gong and Yuanshen were both killed. The people of the prefecture installed Jushou as acting commissioner.

units.zh: 初，孟方立之亂，居受以澤、潞歸於武皇，至是孟遷以邢、洺納降，復任為牙將，居受懼其圖己，乃叛，殺克恭以結汴人。
units.en: During Meng Fangli's rebellion Jushou had surrendered Ze and Lu to Li Keyong. Now Meng Qian surrendered Xing and Ming and was reappointed a garrison officer. Fearing that Meng Qian would move against him, Jushou rebelled, killed Ke Gong, and sought an alliance with the Liang.
units.literal: Earlier, during Meng Fangli's rebellion, Jushou had surrendered Ze and Lu to the Martial Emperor. Now Meng Qian surrendered Xing and Ming and was reappointed a garrison officer. Jushou feared he would plot against him, therefore rebelled and killed Ke Gong to ally with the Bian.

units.zh: 居受遣人召馮霸於沁水，霸不受命。
units.en: Jushou sent men to summon Feng Ba at Qinshui, but Feng Ba refused to obey.
units.literal: Jushou sent men to summon Feng Ba at Qinshui, but Ba refused the order.

units.zh: 居受懼，將奔歸朝廷，至長子，為野人所殺，傳首馮霸軍。
units.en: Terrified, Jushou set out to flee to the Tang court. At Changzi he was killed by local bandits, and his head was sent to Feng Ba's camp.
units.literal: Jushou was afraid and was about to flee back to the court. When he reached Changzi he was killed by local bandits, and his head was sent to Feng Ba's army.

units.zh: 霸乃引軍據潞州，自稱留後，求援於汴。
units.en: Feng Ba then seized Luzhou, declared himself acting commissioner, and appealed to the Liang for help.
units.literal: Ba then led his army to occupy Luzhou, styled himself acting commissioner, and sought aid from Bian.

units.zh: 武皇令康君立討之，汴將葛從周來援霸。
units.en: Li Keyong ordered Kang Junli to suppress him. The Liang general Ge Congzhou marched to Feng Ba's relief.
units.literal: The Martial Emperor ordered Kang Junli to attack him. The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to relieve Ba.

units.zh: 九月，李存孝急攻潞州，汴軍夜遁，獲霸等誅之，武皇乃以康君立為昭義節度使。
units.en: In the ninth month Li Cunxiao pressed the attack on Luzhou. The Liang army fled by night, Feng Ba and his fellows were captured and executed, and Li Keyong appointed Kang Junli military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: In the ninth month Li Cunxiao pressed the attack on Luzhou. The Bian army fled by night. Ba and the others were captured and executed, and the Martial Emperor then appointed Kang Junli military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 克寧，武皇之季弟也。
units.en: Ke Ning was Li Keyong's youngest brother.
units.literal: Ke Ning was the Martial Emperor's youngest brother.

units.zh: 初從起雲中，為奉誠軍使，赫連鐸之攻黃花城也，克寧奉武皇及諸弟登城，血戰三日，力盡備竭，殺賊萬計。
units.en: He had followed Li Keyong from the first rising in Yunzhong and served as commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. When Helian Duo attacked Huanghua Fort, Ke Ning helped Li Keyong and his brothers onto the walls. For three days they fought hand to hand until strength and supplies were spent, killing rebels by the tens of thousands.
units.literal: From the first he followed the rise in Yunzhong and was commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. When Helian Duo attacked Huanghua Fort, Ke Ning attended the Martial Emperor and his brothers onto the walls. For three days they fought in blood; strength and supplies were exhausted, and rebels slain numbered in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 燕軍之攻蔚州，克寧昆仲嬰城拒敵，晝夜輟寢食者旬餘。
units.en: When the Yan army besieged Weizhou, Ke Ning and his brothers held the city and went more than ten days and nights with scarcely any sleep or food.
units.literal: When the Yan army attacked Weizhou, Ke Ning and his brothers held the city and resisted the enemy, going more than ten days and nights without sleep or food.

units.zh: 後從達靼入關，逐黃寇。
units.en: Later he marched through the passes with the Tatar allies and drove off Huang Chao's forces.
units.literal: Later he followed the Tatars into the passes and drove off the Huang bandits.

units.zh: 凡征行無不衛從，於昆弟之間，最推仁孝，小心恭謹，武皇尤友愛之。
units.en: On every campaign he marched at Li Keyong's side. Among the brothers he was the most noted for kindness and filial devotion, careful and deferential in manner, and Li Keyong cherished him above the rest.
units.literal: On every campaign he was never absent as escort. Among the brothers he was most esteemed for benevolence and filial piety, careful and reverent, and the Martial Emperor especially cherished him.

units.zh: 及鎮太原，授遼州刺史，累至雲州防禦使。
units.en: When Li Keyong held Taiyuan, Ke Ning was made prefect of Liaozhou and later promoted to defender of Yunzhou.
units.literal: When he held Taiyuan he was appointed prefect of Liaozhou and was promoted in succession to defender of Yunzhou.

units.zh: 乾寧初，改忻州刺史，從入關討王行瑜，充馬步軍都將，以功授檢校司徒。
units.en: Early in the Qianning era he was made prefect of Xinzhou. He followed Li Keyong through the passes against Wang Xingyu as commander-in-chief of horse and foot and, for his service, was appointed acting minister of education.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he was transferred to prefect of Xinzhou. Following the entry into the passes to attack Wang Xingyu, he served as commander-in-chief of horse and foot and, for merit, was appointed acting minister of education.

units.zh: 天祐初，授內外都製置、管內蕃漢都知兵馬使、檢校太保，充振武節度使，凡軍政皆決於克寧。
units.en: Early in the Tianyou era he was made overall commissioner for inner and outer affairs, commander of all Tangut and Chinese forces in the circuit, acting grand guardian, and military commissioner of Zhenwu. Military and civil affairs alike were left to Ke Ning's decision.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was appointed overall commissioner for inner and outer affairs, commander of all Tangut and Chinese military forces within the circuit, acting grand guardian, and military commissioner of Zhenwu. All military and civil affairs were decided by Ke Ning.

units.zh: 五年正月，武皇疾篤，克寧等侍疾，垂泣辭訣。
units.en: In the first month of the fifth year Li Keyong fell gravely ill. Ke Ning and the others kept vigil at his bedside, weeping as they bade him farewell.
units.literal: In the first month of the fifth year the Martial Emperor's illness was grave. Ke Ning and the others attended his sickbed, weeping as they took leave.

units.zh: 克寧曰：「王萬一不諱，後事何屬？」
units.en: Ke Ning said, "If anything should happen to you, my lord, who is to take charge of what follows?"
units.literal: Ke Ning said, "If Your Majesty should meet with misfortune, to whom should later affairs belong?"

units.zh: 因召莊宗侍側，謂克寧、張承業曰：「亞子累公等。」
units.en: He then had Emperor Zhuangzong brought to his side and said to Ke Ning and Zhang Chengye, "Yazi will be a burden on you all."
units.literal: He then summoned Emperor Zhuangzong to attend at his side and said to Ke Ning and Zhang Chengye, "Yazi burdens you all."

units.zh: 言終棄代。
units.en: With those words he died.
units.literal: When he had finished speaking he passed from this generation.

units.zh: 將發哀，克寧紀綱軍府，中外無嘩。
units.en: As mourning was proclaimed, Ke Ning took command of the military government, and neither within the yamen nor outside it was there any disturbance.
units.literal: When mourning was about to be proclaimed, Ke Ning commanded the military government, and within and without there was no uproar.

units.zh: 初，武皇獎勵軍戎，多畜庶孽，衣服禮秩如嫡者六七輩，比之嗣王，年齒又長，各有部曲，朝夕聚謀，皆欲為亂。
units.en: Li Keyong had long rewarded his officers by raising many sons by concubines. Six or seven of them were dressed and honored like legitimate heirs. They were older than the designated successor and each commanded his own following. Day and night they met to plot rebellion.
units.literal: Earlier the Martial Emperor, rewarding military service, had raised many sons by concubines. Six or seven were treated in dress and ritual rank like legitimate heirs. Compared with the heir, they were also older in years. Each had his own following; morning and evening they gathered to plot, all wishing to make trouble.

units.zh: 莊宗英察，懼及於禍，將嗣位，讓克寧曰：「兒年孤稚，未通庶政，雖承遺命，恐未能彈壓大事。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong was sharp-witted and feared for his life. As he was about to succeed, he offered the position to Ke Ning, saying, "I am young and alone, with no experience of government. Though I have my father's last command, I doubt I can hold the great affairs together.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was keen and perceptive and feared disaster. About to succeed to the throne, he yielded to Ke Ning, saying, "Your servant is young and alone, ignorant of common administration. Though I receive the final command, I fear I cannot suppress great affairs.

units.zh: 季父勳德俱高，眾情推伏，且請製置軍府，候兒有立，聽季父處分。」
units.en: Your merit and standing are high, and everyone looks to you. Please take charge of the military government for now. When I am fit to rule, I will leave everything to you, uncle."
units.literal: Uncle's merit and virtue are both high, and public sentiment defers to you. I beg you to take charge of the military government. When your servant is established, let Uncle decide as he will."

units.zh: 克寧曰：「亡兄遺命，屬在我兒，孰敢異議者！
units.en: Ke Ning replied, "My late brother's last command placed everything in my nephew's hands. Who would dare object!
units.literal: Ke Ning said, "My late brother's final command entrusted affairs to my son. Who would dare raise objection!

units.zh: 兒但嗣世，中外之事，何憂不辦。」
units.en: Nephew, take the succession. Affairs within and without the realm will be managed—have no fear of that."
units.literal: Son, simply succeed to the inheritance. As for affairs within and without, what worry that they cannot be managed."

units.zh: 視事之日，率先拜賀。
units.en: On the day Zhuangzong took office, Ke Ning was the first to bow in congratulation.
units.literal: On the day he assumed office, Ke Ning was first to bow in congratulation.

units.zh: 莊宗嗣位，軍民政事，一切委之，權柄既重，趣向者多附之。
units.en: After Zhuangzong succeeded, he entrusted all military and civil affairs to Ke Ning. As Ke Ning's power grew, ambitious men flocked to his side.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded, military and civil affairs were wholly entrusted to him. Once his authority was weighty, many who sought advancement attached themselves to him.

units.zh: 李存顥者，以陰計幹克寧曰：「兄亡弟及，古今舊事，委父拜侄，理所未安，富貴功名，當宜自立，天與不取，後悔無及。」
units.en: Li Cunhao secretly urged Ke Ning, saying, "When the elder brother dies the younger brother succeeds—that is the old way of the world. For an uncle to bow to his nephew is unnatural. You should seize fortune and rank for yourself. If heaven offers and you refuse, you will regret it when it is too late."
units.literal: Li Cunhao, by secret stratagem, importuned Ke Ning, saying, "When the elder brother dies the younger succeeds—an ancient precedent. For an uncle to yield to a nephew and bow to him is by reason unsettling. Wealth, honor, and achievement should be seized for oneself. Heaven gives and one does not take—later there will be no remorse in time."

units.zh: 克寧曰：「公毋得不祥之言，
units.en: Ke Ning said, "Do not speak such ill-omened words!
units.literal: Ke Ning said, "Sir, do not speak such ill-omened words!

units.zh: 我家世立功三代，父慈子孝，天下知名，苟吾兄山河有托，我亦何求！
units.en: Our house has served with distinction for three generations, father and sons loving and filial, known throughout the realm. If my brother's heir holds the realm in trust, what more could I want!
units.literal: In our house merit has been achieved for three generations; father is kind and sons filial, renowned throughout the realm. If my brother has the realm entrusted to him, what more do I seek!

units.zh: 公無復言，必斬爾首以徇。」
units.en: Say no more of this, or I shall behead you as a warning to others."
units.literal: Sir, speak no more of this, or I shall certainly behead you as a warning."

units.zh: 克寧雖慈愛因心，而日為凶徒惑亂。
units.en: Though Ke Ning was by nature loving and kind, day by day the conspirators led him further astray.
units.literal: Though Ke Ning was by nature loving and kind, day by day he was confused and led astray by wicked men.

units.zh: 群凶之妻復以此言幹克寧妻孟夫人，說激百端，夫人懼事泄及禍，屢讓克寧，由是愈惑。
units.en: The conspirators' wives used the same arguments on Ke Ning's wife, Lady Meng, pressing her from every angle. Fearing exposure and ruin, she repeatedly urged Ke Ning to act, and he grew only more unsettled.
units.literal: The wives of the wicked men again used these words to importune Lady Meng, Ke Ning's wife, urging her with every sort of argument. The lady feared the affair would leak out and bring disaster, and repeatedly reproached Ke Ning, whereby he became all the more confused.

units.zh: 會克寧因事殺都虞候李存質，又請兼領大同節度，以蔚、朔為屬郡，又數怒監軍張承業、李存璋；
units.en: Ke Ning then killed the chief controller Li Cunzhi on a pretext, asked to take the Datong commission as well with Wei and Shuo as subordinate prefectures, and repeatedly provoked the army supervisors Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang;
units.literal: Then Ke Ning, on a pretext, killed the chief controller Li Cunzhi, also requested to hold concurrently the military commission of Datong with Wei and Shuo as subordinate prefectures, and repeatedly angered the army supervisors Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang;

units.zh: 由是知其有貳。
units.en: and from this they knew he was turning disloyal.
units.literal: thereby they knew he was disloyal.

units.zh: 近臣史敬鎔素與存顥善，盡知其事。
units.en: The close attendant Shi Jingrong was an old friend of Cunhao's and knew the whole plot.
units.literal: The close attendant Shi Jingrong had long been on good terms with Cunhao and knew the whole affair.

units.zh: 敬鎔告貞簡太后曰：「存顥與管內太保陰圖叛亂，俟嗣王過其第即擒之，並太后子母，欲送於汴州。
units.en: Jingrong told Empress Dowager Zhenjian, "Cunhao and the circuit grand guardian are secretly plotting rebellion. They mean to seize the heir when he passes their residence, and send you and your son to Bianzhou as well.
units.literal: Jingrong reported to Empress Dowager Zhenjian, saying, "Cunhao and the circuit grand guardian within the command are secretly plotting rebellion. When the heir passes their residence they will seize him, and together with the Empress Dowager mother and son they intend to send them to Bianzhou.

units.zh: 竊發有日矣。」
units.en: The rising is only days away."
units.literal: Their secret rising is only days away."

units.zh: 莊宗召張承業、李存璋謂曰：「季父所為如此，無猶子之情，骨肉不可自相魚肉，吾即避路，則禍亂不作矣。」
units.en: Zhuangzong summoned Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang and said, "My uncle has acted as though he felt no bond between us. Kin must not tear one another apart. I will step aside at once, and the realm will be spared this disaster."
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong summoned Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang and said, "Uncle's conduct is such that he has no feeling of an uncle toward his nephew. Flesh and bone must not devour one another. I shall at once yield the way, and then calamity and disorder will not arise."

units.zh: 承業曰：「老夫親承遺托，言猶在耳。
units.en: Chengye replied, "I received your father's last charge in person, and his words are still in my ears.
units.literal: Chengye said, "This old man personally received the final entrustment; the words are still in my ears.

units.zh: 存顥輩欲以太原降賊，王乃何路求生？
units.en: Cunhao and his fellows mean to hand Taiyuan over to the enemy. What path to safety remains for you, my lord?
units.literal: Cunhao and his fellows wish to surrender Taiyuan to the rebels. By what road, Your Majesty, will you seek to live?

units.zh: 不即討除，亡無日矣。」
units.en: Unless you strike at once, ruin will come within days."
units.literal: If you do not immediately suppress and eliminate them, destruction will come within days."

units.zh: 因令吳珙、存璋為之備。
units.en: He then ordered Wu Gong and Cunzhang to prepare.
units.literal: He then ordered Wu Gong and Cunzhang to make preparations.

units.zh: 二月二十日，會諸將於府第，擒存顥、克寧於坐。
units.en: On the twentieth day of the second month he assembled his generals at the residence and seized Cunhao and Ke Ning where they sat.
units.literal: On the twentieth day of the second month he assembled the generals at the prefectural residence and seized Cunhao and Ke Ning in their seats.

units.zh: 莊宗垂泣數之曰：「兒初以軍府讓季父，季父不忍棄先人遺命。
units.en: Zhuangzong wept as he rebuked them, saying, "I first offered the military government to you, uncle, and you would not set aside my father's last command.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong, weeping, reproached them, saying, "Your servant at first yielded the military government to Uncle. Uncle could not bear to abandon our forefather's final command.

units.zh: 今已事定，復欲以兒子母投畀豺虎，季父何忍此心！」
units.en: Now that all is settled, you would cast me and my mother to the wolves. Uncle, how could you bring yourself to this!"
units.literal: Now that affairs are settled, you again wish to cast your servant and his mother to wolves and tigers. Uncle, how can you bear such a heart!"

units.zh: 克寧泣對曰：「蓋讒夫交構，吾復何言！」
units.en: Ke Ning wept in reply, "Slanderers set us at odds. What more can I say!"
units.literal: Ke Ning wept in reply, saying, "It is all slanderers weaving plots together. What more can I say!"

units.zh: 是日，與存顥俱伏法。
units.en: That day he and Cunhao were both executed.
units.literal: That day he and Cunhao were both executed according to law.

units.zh: 克寧仁而無斷，故及於禍。
units.en: Ke Ning was kind-hearted but indecisive, and so came to ruin.
units.literal: Ke Ning was benevolent but lacked resolution, and therefore met with disaster.

units.zh: 〈（案《新唐書·宰相世係表》：嗣昭，國昌有子四人：克恭、克儉、克用、克柔。
units.en: (According to the 《New Book of Tang·Tables of Chancellor Lineages》: Sizhao—Guochang had four sons: Ke Gong, Ke Jian, Ke Yong, and Ke Rou.
units.literal: (According to the 《New Book of Tang·Tables of Chancellor Lineages》: Sizhao—Guochang had four sons: Ke Gong, Ke Jian, Ke Yong, and Ke Rou.

units.zh: 薛史《李嗣昭傳》云：武皇母弟代州刺史克柔之假子也。
units.en: The Xue History 《Biography of Li Sizhao》 says he was the adopted son of Li Keyong's younger uterine brother Ke Rou, prefect of Daizhou.
units.literal: The Xue History 《Biography of Li Sizhao》 says: He was the adopted son of the Martial Emperor's younger brother by the same mother, Ke Rou, prefect of Daizhou.

units.zh: 是克柔為武皇母弟。
units.en: Thus Ke Rou was Li Keyong's younger uterine brother.
units.literal: Thus Ke Rou was the Martial Emperor's younger brother by the same mother.

units.zh: 《新唐書·沙陀傳》：武皇有弟克勤，《通鑒》引《紀年錄》有兄克儉，而薛史俱無傳，疑有闕文。）〉
units.en: The 《New Book of Tang·Biography of the Shatuo》 records a younger brother Ke Qin. The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 cites the 《Chronicle Record》 as mentioning an elder brother Ke Jian, yet the Xue History has biographies for neither; text may be missing.)〉
units.literal: The 《New Book of Tang·Biography of the Shatuo》: The Martial Emperor had a younger brother Ke Qin. The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 cites the 《Chronicle Record》 as having an elder brother Ke Jian, yet the Xue History has biographies for neither; it is suspected that text is missing.)〉

units.zh: 史臣曰：昔武皇發跡於陰山，莊宗肇基於河朔，雖奄有天下，而享國日淺，眷言枝屬，空秀棣華，固未及推帝堯敦敘之恩，廣成王封建之義。
units.en: The historiographer writes: The Martial Emperor rose from the Yin Mountains and Emperor Zhuangzong founded his rule in Hebei. Though they briefly held the realm, their dynasties were short-lived. Their kinsmen bloomed like catalpa blossoms yet bore no fruit—they never attained Emperor Yao's generous ordering of kin or broadly extended King Cheng's principles of enfeoffment.
units.literal: The historiographer remarks: In former times the Martial Emperor rose from the Yin Mountains and Emperor Zhuangzong founded his rule in Hebei. Though they briefly held all under Heaven, their enjoyment of the realm was brief. Turning affection to the branch kin, the flowering of the catalpa alone was empty show. They indeed did not reach the point of extending Emperor Yao's generous ordering of kin, or of broadly extending King Cheng's principle of enfeoffment.

units.zh: 自克讓而下，不獲就魯、衛之封，懋間、平之德也。
units.en: From Ke Rang downward, none received fiefs like the states of Lu and Wei, nor did they cultivate the virtue of the Princes of Hejian and Dongping.
units.literal: From Ke Rang downward, they did not obtain enfeoffment like Lu and Wei, nor did they display the virtue of Jian and Ping (the Princes of Hejian and Dongping).

units.zh: 況夭橫相繼，亦良可悲哉！
units.en: To make matters worse, violent early deaths followed one after another—a truly lamentable fate!
units.literal: Moreover, untimely violent deaths followed one upon another—truly a matter for deep grief!

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 盧龍軍節度使劉守光封河間郡王；
units.en: Liu Shouguang, military governor of Lulong, was enfeoffed Prince of Hejian;
units.literal: Liu Shouguang, military governor of Lulong, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian;

units.zh: 《通鑒》：七月，岐王與邠涇二帥各遣使告晉，請合兵攻定難節度使李仁福，晉王遣振武節度使周德威將兵會之，合五萬眾，圍夏州。
units.en: 《Zizhi Tongjian》 records: In the seventh month the Prince of Qi and the Bin and Jing governors asked Jin for a joint attack on Li Renfu of Dingnan; the Prince of Jin sent Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu with fifty thousand men to besiege Xia.
units.literal: 《Zizhi Tongjian》: In the seventh month the Prince of Qi and the military governors of Bin and Jing each sent envoys to report to Jin, requesting combined armies to attack Dingnan military governor Li Renfu; the Prince of Jin sent Zhenwu military governor Zhou Dewei to lead troops to join them—altogether fifty thousand, besieging Xia Prefecture.

units.zh: 初，劉知俊誘沙陀振武賊帥周德威、涇原賊帥李繼鸞合步騎五萬大舉，欲俯拾夏台，節度使李仁福兵力俱乏，以急來告。
units.en: Zhijun had drawn Shatuo Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu and Li Jiluan of Jingyuan with fifty thousand horse and foot, thinking Xia would fall at a touch; Li Renfu was spent and cried for help.
units.literal: Initially Liu Zhijun induced Shatuo Zhenwu rebel leader Zhou Dewei and Jingyuan rebel leader Li Jiluan to combine infantry and cavalry fifty thousand in a great advance, intending to pick up Xia Terrace easily; military governor Li Renfu’s strength was entirely lacking and he reported in urgency.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 伏請自貞簡太后升祔禮畢，應宗廟伎樂及群祀，並準舊施行。」
units.en: We respectfully request that from the completion of the enshrinement rites for Empress Dowager Zhenjian, temple music and all group sacrifices should follow the old practice."
units.literal: Your subjects respectfully request that from the completion of the enshrinement rites for Empress Dowager Zhenjian, temple music and all group sacrifices should all follow the old practice."

units.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。
units.en: Ge Congzhou of Bian came to his relief and encamped on the Huan River.
units.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to his aid and encamped at the Huan River.

units.zh: 李克用子落落時爲鐵林軍使，爲從周所擒，乃退歸。
units.en: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and Taiyuan withdrew.
units.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was then Iron Forest Army commander; he was captured by Congzhou and Taiyuan then withdrew.

units.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。
units.en: Ge Congzhou marched in from Xing and Ming.
units.literal: Ge Congzhou led troops from Xing and Ming into Wei.

units.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。
units.en: Congzhou came out to strike in concert, crushed the Yan army, and took thirty thousand heads.
units.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a converging strike and annihilated the Yan army, beheading thirty thousand.

units.zh: 乾寧二年，建與鳳翔李茂貞、邠州王行瑜舉兵赴闕，迫昭宗請以王珙為河中帥，害大臣於都下。
units.en: In Qianning 2 Jian joined Li Maozhen of Fengxiang and Wang Xingyu of Binzhou in marching troops to the capital. They pressured Emperor Zhaozong to appoint Wang Gong military governor of Hezhong and killed senior ministers in the capital.
units.literal: In Qianning year 2 Jian with Fengxiang's Li Maozhen and Binzhou's Wang Xingyu raised troops to the capital, forced Zhaozong to make Wang Gong Hezhong commander, and killed great ministers in the capital.

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 其後，李罕之請以上黨來歸，為晉軍所圍。
units.en: Later Li Hanzhi offered to surrender Shangdang but was besieged by Jin forces.
units.literal: Afterward Li Hanzhi requested to submit Shangdang and return to allegiance, but was besieged by Jin troops.

units.zh: 天復元年，岐、隴用兵，晉人乘虛侵於北鄙。
units.en: In Tianfu 1, while war raged at Qi and Long, Jin raiders struck the northern border.
units.literal: In Tianfu year 1, troops were used at Qi and Long; Jin men took advantage of emptiness to invade the northern frontier.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 時鎔童幼，求援於燕；
units.en: Rong was still young and appealed to Yan for help.
units.literal: At that time Rong was still a child and sought aid from Yan.

units.zh: 鎔以匡威再來援己，致其失師，遣使迎歸府第，父事之。
units.en: Because Kuangwei had twice come to his aid and twice cost him his army, Rong sent envoys to welcome him to his mansion and treated him with the deference due a father.
units.literal: Rong, because Kuangwei had twice come to aid him and thereby caused the loss of his army, sent envoys to welcome him back to the mansion and treated him as a father.

units.zh: 匡威為鎔城郛繕甲，指陳方略，視鎔如子。
units.en: Kuangwei fortified Rong's walls, readied his armor, laid out strategy, and treated Rong as a son.
units.literal: Kuangwei fortified the walls and readied armor for Rong, laid out strategy, and regarded Rong as a son.

units.zh: 會鎔過匡威第慰忌辰，匡威縞衣裹甲，伏兵劫鎔入牙城。
units.en: When Rong came to Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore mourning garments over his armor and used hidden troops to seize Rong and carry him into the headquarters.
units.literal: When Rong happened to visit Kuangwei's mansion to observe a mourning anniversary, Kuangwei wore hemp mourning garments over armor and with hidden troops seized Rong and carried him into the headquarters.

units.zh: 鎔兵逆戰，燔東偏門，軍士呼噪登屋，矢下如雨。
units.en: Rong's troops fought back, burned the eastern gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the rooftops as arrows fell like rain.
units.literal: Rong's troops fought back, burned the east side gate, and soldiers shouting climbed onto the roofs; arrows fell like rain.

units.zh: 鎔僕墨君和亂中扶鎔登屋免難，而斬匡威以徇。
units.en: In the chaos Rong's servant Mo Junhe helped him climb onto a roof to safety, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed his head.
units.literal: Rong's servant Mo Junhe in the chaos helped Rong climb onto a roof and escape harm, then beheaded Kuangwei and displayed the head.

units.zh: 匡威親率軍應之。
units.en: Kuangwei personally led an army to his aid.
units.literal: Kuangwei personally led an army to respond.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 鎮之三軍，素忠於王氏，惡其所為。
units.en: The three armies of Zhenzhou had long been loyal to the Wang clan and despised his conduct.
units.literal: The three armies of Zhen had long been loyal to the Wang clan and hated what he was doing.

units.zh: 後唐莊宗委張承業以軍，竟立大功，此中豈無人乎。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang entrusted Zhang Chengye with his armies, and Zhang won great merit in the end. Surely capable men can be found among them as well.
units.literal: Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong entrusted Zhang Chengye with armies and he in the end achieved great merit — are there not capable men among them?

units.zh: 時幸臣史敬熔者，亦為克寧所誘，盡得其情，乃來告帝。
units.en: Favored minister Shi Jingrong was drawn in but learned all and warned Cunxu.
units.literal: At that time favored minister Shi Jingrong was also enticed by Kening but learned the whole plot and came to inform the Emperor.

units.zh: 天祐五年春正月，武皇疾篤，召監軍張承業、大將吳珙謂曰：「吾常愛此子志氣遠大，可付後事，惟卿等所教。」
units.en: In the first month of Tianyou 5 Wuhuang lay dying; he called Zhang Chengye and Wu Gong and said, "I have always prized this boy's great spirit—entrust what follows to him and teach him well."
units.literal: In the first month of spring, Tianyou 5, Wuhuang was gravely ill; he summoned monitor Zhang Chengye and great general Wu Gong and said: "I have always loved this child's lofty ambition; later affairs may be entrusted to him—only you must instruct him."

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
